claims.text: A wallet's only essential job is to let you receive and spend duffs: it creates public keys/addresses to receive funds and stores the matching private keys to spend them.
A private key is what unlocks, or spends, the duffs held at a particular address: it creates signatures that others verify with the matching public key.

The private key is the root of control over an address's funds: the public key is derived from it and the address is derived from the public key, so whoever holds the private key can spend whatever that address receives.

Losing a private key or seed means losing the funds it controls permanently; there is no reset or recovery path, and the docs warn that a key generated, used, and then lost before being backed up leaves the stored duffs 'likely lost forever'.

A seed phrase (mnemonic) is a pseudo-sentence of 12 to 24 common words that encodes 128 to 256 bits of entropy and, optionally with a passphrase, is hashed into the wallet's 512-bit root seed (BIP39).
Word count maps directly to entropy: 128 bits gives 12 words, 160 gives 15, 192 gives 18, 224 gives 21, and 256 gives 24.

The root seed is the single thing to back up: it is hashed into the master private key and master chain code, from which the entire tree of child keys and addresses is derived (BIP32 hierarchical deterministic wallet).

Derivation is deterministic: the same seed always produces the same keys and addresses, which is why one backup covers the whole wallet and why separate programs (such as an offline or hardware signing wallet) can independently derive the same keys.
One mnemonic derives both your Core addresses and your identity keys; the Dash SDK performs this derivation for you from the mnemonic plus a derivation path (BIP44 for addresses).
Mainnet is the real network where duffs have real value; testnet is a separate, near-identical network where duffs have no real-world value, letting developers practice safely.

Testnet and mainnet are separate chains whose coins do not move between them; testnet relaxes some restrictions (e.g. standard-transaction checks), is subject to resets/incompatible changes, and its Dash Platform infrastructure (150 masternodes plus DAPI and Drive) is run by Dash Core Group.
Free testnet funds come from a faucet, a service that dispenses testnet Dash that has no real value; you provide an address and it sends you test Dash.
The Platform docs point the testnet faucet at https://faucet.testnet.networks.dash.org/, while the Core docs list the Dash Core Group faucet at https://testnet-faucet.dash.org/.

conflicts.topic: Faucet URL disagrees across vendored doc sets
conflicts.resolution: Teach the Platform docs URL (https://faucet.testnet.networks.dash.org/) as the primary pointer, since it is the pinned Platform 3.1.0 source, and name the Dash Core Group URL (https://testnet-faucet.dash.org/) as the alternative while noting faucets can move or go down.

uncertainties.question: Must module 7 name the address type the faucet sends to, or keep it conceptual?
uncertainties.whyItMatters: Asserting the wrong address type would conflict with module 8, which owns DIP-18 Platform address derivation and the funding path.
uncertainties.resolution: Keep module 7 conceptual: say the faucet sends free testnet Dash to an address the learner provides, and leave the exact address type and DIP-18 funding path to module 8.
